Flooding Hits Electric Utilities' Sites in Northern Spain, Disrupting Operations

Severe flooding triggered by torrential rains is impacting electric utilities across northern Spain, with several power generation plants and network facilities reporting damage and operational disruptions. The event, which began late Sunday and is ongoing, has inundated major river valleys in the regions of Cantabria and the Basque Country, threatening some of the industry’s most critical sites.

Empresa Electricidad del Peru - Electroperu SA confirmed that its hydroelectric plant near the Ebro River has been partially flooded. According to spokesperson Marta Ruiz, “We have implemented emergency protocols and are working to protect essential infrastructure and ensure the safety of our staff. However, some equipment has been submerged, and operations are currently suspended at the affected facility.” Ruiz added that over 60 employees have been relocated from low-lying areas as a precaution.

Other firms, including Energia Norte SA, also reported significant impacts. Energia Norte SA said two of its substation sites in the province of Vizcaya are under water, with technical teams unable to access some control rooms due to high water levels. Company officials stated that site assessments and restoration timelines remain uncertain as the situation continues to evolve.

The Spanish Association of Electric Utilities (Asociación Española de Empresas Eléctricas) highlighted the challenges facing the sector. In a statement, the group noted, “Ongoing flooding is creating hazardous conditions for workers and complicating access to plant sites. Companies are prioritizing staff safety and damage mitigation while monitoring the situation closely.”

Preliminary estimates from industry analysts suggest that direct physical damage to plant infrastructure could run into millions of euros, depending on the duration and extent of the flooding. The full impact on output and operational continuity will depend on how quickly water levels recede and facilities can be safely re-entered and inspected.

With meteorological forecasts predicting further rainfall in the coming days, electric utility operators are preparing for continued disruption and potential escalation. Emergency teams remain on alert, and industry leaders are coordinating closely with local authorities to manage ongoing risks to sites and personnel.
